# CloudWatch Events Rules

The `cloudwatchEvent` event triggers a Lambda function when an event on the default event bus matches a pattern, such as an EC2 instance changing state. CloudWatch Events is the earlier name of Amazon EventBridge: the Framework creates an EventBridge rule on the default event bus with the `cloudwatchEvent` event's pattern, the function as its target, and a permission for EventBridge to invoke the function. For custom event buses, schedules, retry policies and dead-letter queues, use the [`eventBridge` event](./event-bridge.md) instead.

This `serverless.yml` runs a function whenever an EC2 instance enters the `pending` state:

```yaml
# serverless.yml
service: my-service

provider:
  name: aws
  runtime: nodejs24.x

functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
            detail-type:
              - EC2 Instance State-change Notification
            detail:
              state:
                - pending
```

The handler receives the matching event, with the service-specific data in `event.detail`:

```javascript
// handler.mjs
export const instanceStateChange = async (event) => {
  console.log(
    event['detail-type'],
    event.detail['instance-id'],
    event.detail.state,
  )
}
```

## cloudwatchEvent event options

The `cloudwatchEvent` event accepts these keys:

| Key                | Type                                            | Default                                  | Description                                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `event`            | object                                          | Required                                 | The event pattern the rule matches           |
| `enabled`          | boolean                                         | `true`                                   | Whether the rule is enabled                  |
| `name`             | string, 1–64 characters                         | Generated by CloudFormation              | The rule name                                |
| `description`      | string, up to 512 characters                    | No description                           | The rule description                         |
| `input`            | object, or JSON string up to 8,192 characters   | Not set: the function receives the event | A fixed payload passed instead of the event  |
| `inputPath`        | JSONPath string, 1–256 characters               | Not set                                  | The part of the event passed to the function |
| `inputTransformer` | object with `inputTemplate` and `inputPathsMap` | Not set                                  | A payload built from values in the event     |

## Event patterns

The `cloudwatchEvent` event's `event` key is an EventBridge event pattern, written in YAML. The rule matches an event when every field in the pattern matches; a list matches any of its values. The pattern in the preceding example matches EC2 state-change events with the state `pending`.

Patterns also accept content filters, such as `prefix`, `anything-but` and `numeric`. This pattern matches every EC2 state change except to `running`:

```yaml
functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
            detail-type:
              - EC2 Instance State-change Notification
            detail:
              state:
                - anything-but: running
```

For the pattern syntax, see [Amazon EventBridge event patterns](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-event-patterns.html). For the events each AWS service sends, see [Events from AWS services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events.html).

## Input, input path and input transformer

By default, the function receives the whole event. To pass something else, set one of `input`, `inputPath` or `inputTransformer` on the `cloudwatchEvent` event; set at most one of them per event.

`input` passes a fixed payload instead of the event. An object is converted to JSON:

```yaml
functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
          input:
            stage: dev
            action: audit
```

`inputPath` passes the part of the event that a JSONPath selects:

```yaml
functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
          inputPath: '$.detail'
```

`inputTransformer` builds a payload from values in the event. `inputPathsMap` names the values with JSONPath, and `inputTemplate` (required) uses them as `<name>` placeholders:

```yaml
functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
          inputTransformer:
            inputPathsMap:
              instance: '$.detail.instance-id'
              eventTime: '$.time'
            inputTemplate: '{"instance": "<instance>", "time": "<eventTime>"}'
```

Put a placeholder in quotes when its value is a string, so the result is valid JSON. For the template rules, see [Amazon EventBridge input transformation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-transform-target-input.html).

## Rule name and description

The `cloudwatchEvent` event's `name` and `description` set the rule's name and description:

```yaml
functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          name: ec2-pending-instances
          description: Runs when an EC2 instance enters the pending state
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
            detail-type:
              - EC2 Instance State-change Notification
            detail:
              state:
                - pending
```

- `name`: 1 to 64 characters, using only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`. It must be unique among the rules on the default event bus in the Region, so a fixed name stops you from deploying the same service to two stages in one Region; include the stage, as in `ec2-pending-${sls:stage}`. Without `name`, CloudFormation generates a unique name.
- `description`: up to 512 characters.

See [PutRule](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/APIReference/API_PutRule.html) for the rule name rules.

## Disable a rule

A `cloudwatchEvent` rule is enabled by default. To deploy the rule without triggering the function, set `enabled: false`:

```yaml
functions:
  instanceStateChange:
    handler: handler.instanceStateChange
    events:
      - cloudwatchEvent:
          enabled: false
          event:
            source:
              - aws.ec2
```

## Permissions for CloudWatch Events rules

For each `cloudwatchEvent` event, the Framework adds a `lambda:InvokeFunction` permission for `events.amazonaws.com`, limited to the rule's ARN. The function's execution role needs no extra permissions to receive events.

## Troubleshooting CloudWatch Events rules

### `You can only set one of input, inputPath, or inputTransformer properties at the same time for cloudwatch events. ...`

This happens when one `cloudwatchEvent` event sets more than one of `input`, `inputPath` and `inputTransformer`. Keep one of them; to send the same events with different payloads, add a second `cloudwatchEvent` event with the same `event` pattern.
